source_text.Q-1040: LOW, test-only, CI/test lane. test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs polling loops at ~L518 and ~L817 (Enum.reduce_while(1..20) with Process.sleep(10) = ~200 ms of observation) wait for a supervised Lua child while the script/call runs only timeout_ms 300; under host load the child can finish or not yet have started inside that window, so the assertion that a real in-flight child was observed can miss it. Fix: make the script deterministic instead of time-bound (script blocks on a message from the test, or the poll waits on a :started message plus a monotonic deadline well above the script's life; the script's duration is controlled by the test, not a sleep) so the window cannot close before the test looks; no global timing change. Mutation proof: a mutant that never spawns the child must still fail; stress: 100 consecutive runs under max_cases concurrency green (quote command and result). Acceptance: (1) both observation windows no longer depend on a fixed ~200 ms poll inside a 300 ms script; (2) mutant that never spawns the child still fails both tests; (3) 100 consecutive local runs under concurrency green, command and result quoted. Overlap: no open queue issue on executor_test; ISS-0456 (wasm_hang) is a different file. GH #2379.

result.summary: Test-only diff (git diff a3b95f0eb..HEAD --stat: executor_test.exs, docs/anti-patterns.md, handoffs; no lib/ change). SECURITY-REVIEWER gate N/A. Idiomatic: own-child lookup via $callers is the supported Task bookkeeping; Process.info(pid,:dictionary) returning nil for a child that exited between children/1 and inspection is handled by the nil -> false clause; monotonic deadline replaces attempt-count polling; kill ends the script deterministically. Dropped {:wallclock_timeout,300} assertion remains covered by executor_test.exs:420 (and the other :lua_wallclock_race tests). Exact :killed string matches executor.ex:566/662 format ("#{inspect(__MODULE__)} task crashed: " <> format_exit_reason). No leak: helper returns nil only when no own child exists; a pid is killed immediately, and caller Task.async is linked to the test. No scope creep (one private helper, no new behaviours/macros, no global timing change); no decision-record conflict; no type-safety gaps; anti-patterns entry is accurate and non-duplicative.

findings.text: await_own_child/2 inspects every child of the named supervisor each 5 ms for up to 5 s; fine for a test, but if the supervisor ever hosts many children the helper is O(n) per poll. No action needed.
timeout_ms: 30_000 is a ceiling; if the kill path were ever removed the test would hold a spinning child up to 30 s. Current code always kills on the is_pid path, so no leak today.
